claim: Every strong semantic relation can be represented by Hamming-1 adjacency in one binary cube.
scope: Any fixed-width hypercube used as the complete semantic-relation graph.
minimal_counterexample: Strong triangle: ()--ATOM, ()--CONS, ATOM--CONS; hypercubes are bipartite/triangle-free.
remains_open: Hamming/prefix geometry may still be useful as address structure or inside a separately proven local family.

claim: Unordered direct seed-support is sufficient to choose a unique semantic prefix parent.
minimal_counterexample: CADR and CDAR both have unordered support {CAR,CDR}, but ordered paths are 1011 and 1100 with different roots.
remains_open: Typed ordered generators may still justify prefix edges.

claim: Named call/dependency depth is a refactoring-invariant semantic rank.
scope: Any ranking that counts named helper layers before semantic normalization.
minimal_counterexample: CAR(CDR(x)) and CAR(tail(x)) with tail(y)=CDR(y) are semantically equal but the helper-factored named graph adds a layer.
remains_open: Normalized derivation cost remains open and is researched in #1969/#2002.

claim: Transitive derivability/seed-support alone is sufficient to rank or identify derived semantics.
minimal_counterexample: APPEND and PAIR (Lisp I) expand to the same seven-seed support set while denoting different operations; evaluator helpers also collapse onto shared full support.
remains_open: Seed-support remains useful as dependency evidence, not semantic identity/rank.

claim: Evaluator SCC topology is stable enough across historical realizations to determine semantic identity/domain placement.
scope: Lisp I vs Lisp 1.5 bounded evaluator corpus.

claim: The semantic 00 separator can also act as a raw in-band delimiter for unrestricted variable-width words.
scope: Packed raw bitstream with no external token framing.
minimal_counterexample: Word 0001 contains 00 internally; source token sequence 10 | 0001 | 01 cannot be recovered by splitting raw concatenation on 00.
remains_open: 00 remains a semantic/source boundary identity; transport may carry boundaries out-of-band/with length framing.

claim: NULL, EQUAL, or MEMBER already justify immediate selector-strength EQ children 0110/0111.
scope: The bounded NULL/EQUAL/MEMBER candidates under the fixed local composition/no-new-control/no-recursion criterion.
minimal_counterexample: NULL is not EQ-direct; EQUAL imports ATOM/CAR/CDR/COND plus recursion; MEMBER is recursive multi-root traversal.
remains_open: A richer typed EQ algebra may still exist; #2013 owns that search.

claim: LIST/APPEND/PAIR/PAIRLIS already justify immediate selector-strength CONS children.
scope: Bounded Lisp I/Lisp 1.5 named construction-helper candidates.
minimal_counterexample: LIST needs CONS+NIL and changes arity; APPEND/PAIR/PAIRLIS import multiple roots and/or recursion/control.
remains_open: A smaller algebraic CONS generator may still exist; #2014 owns that search.

claim: Predicate AND/OR are valid immediate local COND children under current two-part COND and PredicateBit semantics.
scope: Current answer-contract/2 where exhaustion=() and PredicateBit false=0.
minimal_counterexample: AND(0,0) and AND(0,1) yield () instead of 0; OR(0,0) yields () instead of 0.
remains_open: Other COND specializations that preserve () != 0 may still exist; #2015 owns that search.

claim: Function identity must be a flat exact-8-bit 256-peer semantic universe.
minimal_counterexample: No logical counterexample is claimed here; the premise was intentionally superseded by variable-width research and kept only as compatibility/backend donor evidence.
remains_open: Whether a particular backend keeps an 8-bit projection remains an engineering question.
